title.en: Steps a bill goes through, and why voting matters
title.fr: Les étapes d'un projet de loi, et l'importance du vote

text.en: A bill is examined in both chambers. The House of Commons studies it, and so does the Senate.
text.fr: Un projet de loi est examiné dans les deux chambres. La Chambre des communes l'étudie, et le Sénat aussi.

source.quote: Both the House of Commons and the Senate consider and review bills

verification.evidence: Both the House of Commons and the Senate consider and review bills (proposals for new laws).

text.en: A bill is a proposal for a new law.
text.fr: Un projet de loi est une proposition de nouvelle loi.

source.quote: consider and review bills (proposals for new laws).

text.en: A bill becomes law only after both chambers pass it and it receives royal assent. The Governor General gives royal assent on behalf of the Sovereign.
text.fr: Un projet de loi devient une loi seulement après avoir été adopté par les deux chambres et avoir reçu la sanction royale. Le gouverneur général donne la sanction royale au nom du souverain.

source.quote: No bill can become law in Canada until it has been passed by both chambers and has received royal assent, granted by the Governor General on behalf of the Sovereign.

text.en: Step one is first reading. The bill is treated as read for the first time, and it is printed.
text.fr: La première étape est la première lecture. Le projet de loi est considéré comme lu une première fois, et il est imprimé.

source.quote: First Reading – The bill is considered read for the first STEP 1 time and is printed.

text.en: At second reading, members debate the main idea behind the bill.
text.fr: À la deuxième lecture, les députés débattent du principe du projet de loi.

source.quote: Second Reading – Members debate the bill’s principle.

text.en: At the committee stage, the members of a committee study the bill one clause at a time.
text.fr: À l'étape du comité, les membres d'un comité étudient le projet de loi article par article.

source.quote: Committee Stage – Committee members study the bill STEP 3 clause by clause.

text.en: At the report stage, members can propose other changes to the bill.
text.fr: À l'étape du rapport, les députés peuvent proposer d'autres modifications au projet de loi.

source.quote: Report Stage – Members can make other amendments.

verification.evidence: STEP 4 Report Stage – Members can make other amendments.

text.en: At third reading, members debate the bill and then vote on it.
text.fr: À la troisième lecture, les députés débattent du projet de loi, puis votent.

source.quote: Third Reading – Members debate and vote on the bill.

verification.evidence: STEP 5 Third Reading – Members debate and vote on the bill.

text.en: Next, the bill goes to the Senate, where it goes through much the same steps.
text.fr: Ensuite, le projet de loi passe au Sénat, où il suit à peu près les mêmes étapes.

source.quote: Senate – The bill follows a similar process in the Senate.

text.en: Royal assent is step seven. A bill receives it once both Houses have passed it.
text.fr: La sanction royale est la septième étape. Un projet de loi la reçoit une fois que les deux chambres l'ont adopté.

source.quote: Royal Assent – The bill receives royal assent after being STEP 7 passed by both Houses.

verification.evidence: STEP 6 Senate – The bill follows a similar process in the Senate. Royal Assent – The bill receives royal assent after being STEP 7 passed by both Houses.

text.en: In a democracy, citizens have a right to help make the decisions that affect them. It is also their responsibility.
text.fr: Dans une démocratie, les citoyens ont le droit de participer aux décisions qui les touchent. C'est aussi leur responsabilité.

source.quote: Living in a democracy, Canadian citizens have the right and the responsibility to participate in making decisions that affect them.

text.en: Canadians who are eighteen or older should take part in their democracy and vote. That means elections at all three levels: municipal, provincial or territorial, and federal.
text.fr: Les Canadiens de dix-huit ans ou plus devraient participer à leur démocratie et voter. Cela vaut pour les élections des trois ordres : municipales, provinciales ou territoriales, et fédérales.

source.quote: It is important for Canadians aged 18 or more to participate in their democracy by voting in federal, provincial or territorial and municipal elections.

verification.evidence: Living in a democracy, Canadian citizens have the right and the responsibility to participate in making decisions that affect them. It is important for Canadians aged 18 or more to participate in their democracy by voting in federal, provincial or territorial and municipal elections.
